problems.title: The first rising-sea event
problems.statement: Carry out one operational rising-sea event in the sense of [S01, Vol. III, §5.1]. Such an event “must begin from an explicit obstruction or language deficit, propose a typed extension, compile bounded probes, preserve or explicitly surrender recovery, record costs and residuals, and submit any status request to authority outside the producing engines.” The problem asks for an event of this kind after which the original difficulty, stated before the event, has become tractable in the extended setting without the question having been changed.
problems.established: The source fixes the sequence obstruction → typed extension → bounded execution and checking → computed, partial or failed → recovery and transport → external request, observes that “Each arrow may fail”, and declines to promote the strategy: “Volume III does not turn that strategy into a universal theorem of problem solving. It turns it into a falsifiable campaign record.” It names four ways in which an extension changes the question instead of answering it: an extension that “deletes the predicate expressing a contradiction, forgets the invariant detecting failure, weakens equality until disagreement disappears, or renames an unknown as a new primitive has not resolved the original obstruction.” Section 5.8 specifies the residual and non-equivalence records that a partial outcome must leave. No event has been carried out.
problems.proposed_by: The image of the rising sea is Grothendieck’s [McL07]; its operational form and this problem are from [S01].
problems.background: [McL07]; [Lak76]; machine-guided discovery with an external evaluator [DVB+21; RBN+24].
problems.solved_when: A campaign record is published that a third party can replay, in which (i) every step of the §5.1 sequence is present as a typed artifact; (ii) the target statement, frozen before the campaign, receives in the extended setting a kernel-checked proof, a kernel-checked refutation, or a reduction to named hypotheses with their statuses recorded; and (iii) a reviewer independent of the producing system certifies that none of the four failures of §5.1 applies. A complete record of a failed campaign is listed as a partial result.

literature_check.finding: No published campaign record of this form was found. Machine-guided discovery systems [DVB+21; RBN+24; TWL+24] evaluate candidates externally but do not record the four failure patterns or a separate status request.

problems.title: A bounded fixed point of the coupled world–language cycle
problems.statement: Give a formal transition model of the coupled world–language cycle of [S01, Vol. III, Ch. 71–78] and prove, in a proof assistant, three properties of it: (a) the obligation-preservation inclusion $O^{\mathrm{open}}_n \subseteq O^{\mathrm{open}}_{n+1} \cup O^{\mathrm{dis}}_{n+1} \cup O^{\mathrm{term}}_{n+1}$ of §75.11 holds for every accepted step; (b) the six conditions of §75.17 under which “A cycle reaches BOUNDED_FIXED_POINT” are decidable from the records; and (c) every run terminates, since “A conforming campaign therefore carries a well-founded repair measure or a hard policy bound.”
problems.established: The conditions are stated as contracts; none is proved. Failure of the inclusion in (a) “is sufficient for refusal or quarantine, regardless of the attractiveness of the new result.” The source limits what a fixed point means: “This is not equality of world and language, global convergence, consistency, optimality, or future stability.”
problems.background: Transition systems and invariants in the style of [HW90]; mechanised metatheory [BW05].
problems.solved_when: A machine-checked development (Lean, Rocq, Isabelle or Agda) that defines the model, documents its correspondence with §§75.11 and 75.17 clause by clause, and proves (a)–(c); or a machine-checked counterexample showing that one of them fails in every model faithful to the source.

literature_check.finding: No formal model of this cycle was found; the searches returned general work on invariants in refinement-based verification only.

problems.title: From obstruction to conjecture
problems.statement: Implement the obstruction-driven conjecture generator ALG-118 of [S01, Vol. IV, Ch. 109], which takes replayable, typed records of failed constructions or proof attempts and returns scoped conjectures, each with at least one executable falsifier, and run it until it produces a conjecture that is then settled by others.
problems.established: The source specifies the contract and its limits: “An obstruction can explain why a particular construction, proof route, or finite experiment failed. It does not by itself establish the negation, necessity, naturalness, or novelty of a conjecture inferred from that failure.” Status is not affected by how a candidate looks: “Frequency, linguistic plausibility, retrieval rank, model agreement, elegance, and apparent usefulness do not change its epistemic status.” Falsifiers are part of the output, and “No finite search can certify an unrestricted conjecture.” No implementation exists.
problems.solved_when: An implementation run on a published set of typed obstructions, with the full record of every candidate and of its falsifiers, such that at least one generated conjecture that is not in the frozen corpus (in the scoped sense of [S01, Vol. IV, §110.8]) is afterwards proved, or refuted by a replayed counterexample, by parties independent of the generator.

literature_check.finding: Theory exploration and conjecturing systems were found [Faj88; RGM+21]; none takes typed obstruction records as input or attaches falsifiers to each output.

problems.title: Minimal extension questions
problems.statement: “MinimalExtensionQuestion turns a diagnosed deficit into an ordered search over semantic deltas.” For a declared class of mathematical worlds and a declared partial order on deltas, give a procedure that, from an independently checked obstruction, returns an extension that is minimal for that order, consistent, conservative over the predecessor world, and reopens the blocked obligation; or prove that no such procedure exists for the class.
problems.established: The question belongs to the Topos New-Creation Architecture (TNCA), the engine of [S01] that proposes successor worlds. The source fixes the meaning of minimality — “Minimality is relative to that declared partial order, not to implementation effort or textual brevity” — and gives the two failure modes it must avoid (jumping to a stronger logic, and refusing an extension that is needed). It states what is missing: “TNCA has not shown existence, consistency, conservativity, or usefulness of any answer.”
problems.background: Conservative extensions in logic and type theory; [Mac78] for the categorical constructions involved.
problems.solved_when: A stated class of worlds (for example finitely axiomatised first-order theories or finite presentations of categories), a declared order on deltas, and a machine-checked proof that the procedure is correct on the class, with an implementation evaluated on published obstructions; or a machine-checked impossibility result for a class of comparable generality.

literature_check.finding: Work on conservative extension and minimal extensions in logic was found; no procedure with the inputs and guarantees of §24.10 was found.

problems.title: Target fidelity

source.title: GAI-MUA: The Grothendieckian Machine
source.locator: Vol. III, §30.10, p. 8574, and §64.17, p. 9294; Architectural Prospectus, p. 7966; Vol. IV, §5.16, p. 9846

problems.statement: A proof kernel checks a proof against a formal statement; it does not check that the formal statement is the mathematics it was meant to express. In the source: “A named, pinned formal kernel may check a proof term against a formal target; target fidelity and publication authority remain separate obligations.” Give a certificate format and checker for the fidelity of a formal statement to a statement in a source text, within a declared fragment of mathematical language and a declared library.
problems.established: The source treats every machine proof as a candidate “until source-target fidelity, kernel replay, and axiom-closure review pass under the same canonical subject key”, and lists among the open obligations of the formal layer to “verify that adapted definitions and rule candidates faithfully reflect the cited locators and declared deltas” and “target-fidelity theorems connecting source constructs to generated declarations”.
problems.proposed_by: [S01]; the question is shared with the autoformalization literature [WJL+22; FLM+26].
problems.solved_when: A certificate format that binds a formal target, a source locator and a declared map of definitions, and a checker that rejects every certificate in a published adversarial suite of statement pairs with deliberately introduced misformalizations (quantifier order, hypothesis loss, changed definitions) while accepting the faithful pairs, with the suite, the checker and the results released for independent replay.

literature_check.finding: Many 2025–2026 preprints measure faithfulness of autoformalization by scores or round-trip tests; none found issues a fidelity certificate of the kind required here.

problems.title: Verified encodings of universal properties
problems.statement: The component MUF-H (Motivic Universal Factorization Algorithm—Hybrid) of [S01] solves universal-property constraints for finite proxies of categories. “A solver that returns a satisfying assignment only proves satisfiability of the encoded finite constraints if the encoding and certificate are independently checked. It does not establish that the encoding captures the intended universal property.” For finite categories given by their composition tables, give an encoding of the statement that a cone (or cocone) is a limit (colimit) of a finite diagram into constraints a solver can decide, and prove the encoding correct.
problems.established: The source requires that “Universality encodings still require an independently checked correspondence between mathematical quantifiers and constraints”, and that existence of mediating maps and their uniqueness be recorded as separate obligations, since “Universality requires a quantified mediating property and generally uniqueness at an explicitly stated identity strength.”
problems.solved_when: A machine-checked theorem that, for every finite diagram in a finite category, the solutions of the encoded constraints correspond bijectively to mediating morphisms and that the uniqueness check is complete, together with a verified checker for solver certificates.

literature_check.finding: General work on constraint solving and finite model finding was found; no verified encoding of universal properties was found.

problems.title: The AURORA-K0 kernel, I: syntax and checking

source.title: GAI-MUA: The Grothendieckian Machine
source.locator: Vol. III, §70.19, pp. 9428–9429 (obligations K0-META-001 to K0-META-009)

problems.statement: Mechanise AURORA-K0, the small formal kernel of the experimental calculus AURORA [S01, Vol. III, Ch. 70], and discharge the first nine obligations of its registry, among them that the “Concrete grammar has unique parsing after canonical Unicode normalization”, that “Substitution preserves K0 typing”, that “Registered reduction preserves typing”, that “Algorithmic checking agrees with declarative K0 rules”, and that the “Definitional equality procedure is decidable for the declared finite fragment”.
problems.established: The registry lists each obligation with the evidence required before its status may change, and rules out the shortcut: “No row may become RECEIPT_BOUND merely because a checker returns success.” No obligation is discharged.
problems.background: The de Bruijn criterion and small kernels [BW05]; [MU21]; [Car24].
problems.solved_when: A development in a proof assistant that defines K0 as in the exact edition of Chapter 70 and proves K0-META-001 to K0-META-009 using no axioms beyond the assistant’s standard ones; a machine-checked counterexample to any item also counts and is recorded as a correction to the source.

literature_check.finding: Mechanised metatheory of type theories is an established field; no mechanisation of K0 was found.

problems.title: The AURORA-K0 kernel, II: a model and relative consistency

source.title: GAI-MUA: The Grothendieckian Machine
source.locator: Vol. III, §70.19, pp. 9428–9429 (obligations K0-META-010 to K0-META-012)

problems.statement: For the kernel K0 of Problem 7, discharge the semantic obligations of the registry: “At least one nontrivial model validates the rules”; “Relative consistency, if pursued”, relative to a named base theory; and “Conservativity over any source theory” for the source theories that the architecture embeds.
problems.established: The registry requires an explicit model construction with independent validation, a proposition-exact metatheorem for relative consistency, and an explicit interpretation with a conservativity proof, and records all three as open.
problems.background: Models of type theory; [Uni13]; conservativity results for extensions of type theory.
problems.solved_when: A machine-checked model of K0 that is not trivial in the sense of §70.19, and machine-checked proofs of relative consistency and of conservativity over at least one named source theory.

literature_check.finding: Mechanised relative-consistency proofs exist for other systems; none for K0 was found.

problems.title: The seven obligations of descent execution
problems.statement: The Grothendieckian Descent Reasoning Architecture (GDRA) of [S01], the layer that executes local-to-global campaigns, exists to prevent one error: “The central architectural error is to convert operational completion into global meaning.” Give a formal transition model of GDRA campaigns and prove the seven properties that §56.15 leaves open: “canonical serialization must preserve identity; every accepted transition must preserve the invariants; forbidden authority effects must be noninterfering; budget events must conserve declared dimensions; event replay must converge to the same eligible head under the stated delivery model; counterevidence closure must be omission-resistant; and adapters must preserve the disjoint failure constructors.”
problems.established: The source states the seven properties and the delivery model (at-least-once delivery with idempotent effects), and records: “None has a supplied mechanized proof.”
problems.solved_when: Machine-checked proofs of all seven properties for a model whose correspondence with Chapter 56 is documented clause by clause, or a machine-checked counterexample to one of them.

literature_check.finding: Noninterference and replay-safety proofs exist for other systems; none for this model was found.

problems.title: Non-self-authorization

source.title: GAI-MUA: The Grothendieckian Machine
source.locator: Vol. V, Proposition 1.3, p. 11913; Proposition 5.1, p. 11940; Proposition 10.1, p. 11979

problems.statement: The rule that machines propose and humans authorise publication is stated in [S01, Vol. V] as three propositions, each conditional on assumptions about capabilities. Proposition 1.3 concludes that “a non-root module cannot, through a conforming Volume V interface, make its own output both authoritative and active”; Proposition 10.1 that “adding a validated evidence edge to an artifact cannot by itself increase the artifact’s epistemic class”. Give a formal model of capabilities, signing and status transitions in which the hypotheses of Propositions 1.3, 5.1 and 10.1 are definitions, and prove the three conclusions.
problems.established: The propositions are argued informally and marked D/O: “The proposition is conditional on correct capability isolation and validator independence; those conditions are test obligations, not assumptions to be hidden.” The negative cases (a worker writing to the status store, a signature detached from the artifact hash) are listed.
problems.solved_when: Machine-checked proofs of the three propositions in a published model, and a test suite showing that each listed negative case is rejected by an implementation conforming to the model.

literature_check.finding: Verified capability machines and separation kernels exist; no formalisation of these three propositions was found.

problems.title: Evolution without authority
problems.statement: A self-improving component may propose changes to itself but must not acquire authority. In [S01, Vol. VI] the obligation reads: “O-V6-11-04 — prove that no composition of EvolutionContract ports reaches signing, promotion, activation, root mutation, or rollback capabilities”. Prove it for a formal model of the evolution interface.
problems.established: In the released architecture “Evolution remains inert: telemetry cannot evaluate candidates, adapt routing, update policy, canary, promote, deploy, or roll back.” The source does not claim more: “Until these obligations are discharged, policy morphisms and version graphs are precise governance objects, not a claim that safe whole-system evolution has been solved.”
problems.background: [SS75]; reward hacking as the failure this obligation guards against [SHKK22].
problems.solved_when: A machine-checked reachability theorem over all finite compositions of the ports of the published EvolutionContract model, with the model’s correspondence to Vol. VI, Ch. 11 documented; or a composition that reaches a forbidden capability.

literature_check.finding: Recent work studies privilege escalation in AI agents empirically; no formal reachability proof for an evolution interface of this kind was found.

problems.title: Deterministic identity across implementations

source.title: GAI-MUA: The Grothendieckian Machine
source.locator: Vol. V, Proposition 2.2, p. 11920, and Proposition 3.2, p. 11927

problems.statement: Build two independent implementations of the canonical serialization and replay profile of [S01, Vol. V] and show that they agree: identical canonical bytes and identifiers for the same artifacts (Proposition 2.2), and identical kernel judgments under identical inputs and environments (Proposition 3.2).
problems.established: Proposition 2.2 is “an interoperability obligation to be tested by cross-language fixtures.” For replay, “A disagreement is a first-class incident”, and “The system does not choose the favorable result by majority vote.” No second implementation exists.
problems.solved_when: Two implementations in different languages by different authors, and a published fixture suite (Unicode normalisation, exact numbers, ordered and unordered collections, extension fields) on which they agree byte for byte, with every disagreement found during development recorded as an incident.

literature_check.finding: Reproducible-builds practice [LZ22] addresses the same property for software artifacts; no implementation of this profile was found.

problems.title: A frozen benchmark for counterexample and proof discovery
problems.statement: Release the first version of the benchmark specified in [S01, Vol. IV, Ch. 113]. “A benchmark is not merely a directory of examples and a script that prints a score.” Before any run, it “must freeze the task, version, population, split, metric, abstention policy, leakage boundary, resource model, and reporting semantics”, and it must separate counterexample tasks into strata A–F and proof tasks into the seven types of §113.12.13.
problems.established: The specification is complete and unexecuted. Its scoring rules include that “Stratum E evaluates whether the system reports bounded unknown honestly; it does not reward a claim that the theorem is true”, and that “Hidden proofs are protected evaluation assets, not canonical solution paths.”
problems.solved_when: A release with the four boundaries of §113.1 frozen by digest, at least one item in every counterexample stratum and every proof-task type, a working challenge process (§113.12.15), and results for at least two systems reported stratum by stratum.

literature_check.finding: Benchmarks for formal and research mathematics exist [ZHP22; FLM+26]; none found has the stratification, the abstention strata or the frozen constitution of Ch. 113.

problems.title: The language forge, end to end
problems.statement: “The language forge follows a deliberately articulated cycle: collect, mine, name, notate, ground, reconstruct, axiomatize, grow, re-encode, and validate.” Run the cycle of [S01, Vol. III, Ch. 41–48] end to end on a published corpus and produce a new notation and language package for a declared mathematical domain, with its metatheoretic obligations discharged.
problems.established: The source specifies each stage and leaves completeness open: “The order organizes a bounded language-formation workflow and leaves completeness as an open research question.” It requires that “Notation earns trust by declaring what it compresses, what it preserves, and what it cannot recover”, and that “An obligation is not promoted because it is conventional for a language family or appears plausible from examples.”
problems.solved_when: A package for a declared domain in which every introduced primitive is linked to the structural motifs and counterexamples that motivated it, whose substitution, preservation and conservativity obligations (§44.16) are machine-checked, and whose round trips (Ch. 43) pass on a held-out set of statements from the domain.

literature_check.finding: Work on mathematical concept formation and on the language of mathematics [Gan13] was found; no end-to-end language-formation system with these obligations was found.

problems.title: A preregistered test of typed base change

source.title: GAI-MUA: The Grothendieckian Machine
source.locator: Vol. I, §11.12, p. 277 (Conjecture V1-CH-011-C001); definitions, pp. 275–276

problems.statement: Test the conjecture of [S01, Vol. I, §11.12]: “For a corpus whose categorical claims are already expressed as finite typed diagrams, requiring an RCP/RCT pair for each use of “base change” will reduce orientation and hypothesis errors relative to an untyped prose baseline.” Here an RCP (relative change passport) records the bases, the base arrow and its variance, and an RCT (relative claim trace) records the status and hypotheses of the claim made after the change (Definitions V1-CH-011-D003 and D004).
problems.established: “This is a falsifiable editorial-engineering conjecture. It requires a preregistered corpus, error taxonomy, reviewers, and comparison protocol; no performance result is claimed here.”
problems.solved_when: A study whose corpus, error taxonomy, reviewer assignment and analysis are registered before data are collected, with independent reviewers, reporting the result in either direction.

literature_check.finding: No study of this question was found.

problems.title: A preregistered test of the four judgments of gluing
problems.statement: Test the conjecture of [S01, Vol. I, §15.12]: “On a preregistered corpus of local-to-global mathematical arguments, mandatory separation of compatibility, effectivity, uniqueness, and property return will reduce false “gluing succeeds” judgments relative to an untyped prose baseline.”
problems.established: “Testing requires fixed cases, independent reviewers, and an error taxonomy; no empirical result is claimed here.”
problems.solved_when: A preregistered study as in Problem 15, reporting the result in either direction.

literature_check.finding: No study of this question was found.

problems.title: A preregistered test of obstruction records
problems.statement: Test the conjecture of [S01, Vol. I, Ch. 17]: “For a fixed benchmark of finite, fully enumerated lifting and gluing problems with independently verified ground truth, requiring the fields of ObstructionRecordV1 will reduce false “no solution” classifications relative to an otherwise identical checker that stores only a Boolean success flag.”
problems.established: “This is an empirical systems conjecture, not a mathematical theorem.” The same section forbids the strengthening that every failed construction determines a cohomology class whose vanishing solves the problem.
problems.solved_when: A preregistered comparison of the two checkers on a published benchmark with enumerated ground truth, reporting the false-negative rates of both with confidence intervals.

literature_check.finding: No study of this question was found.

problems.title: Discovering the site

source.title: GM-Omega-Infinity: Topos-Native Intelligence
source.status: open (listed among “The five things we are least sure of”)

problems.statement: In the architecture of [S02] a context is a site, the information it supports is a sheaf, and a conclusion is a global section. The site itself is supplied by hand: “The site must be imposed. We do not know how to discover the evidence-atom locale from a corpus; we construct it.” Give a procedure that constructs the evidence-atom locale, its refinement order and its covering families from a corpus, with a stated sufficiency criterion, and show that the result does not merely reflect the design of the procedure.
problems.established: The source states the objection it cannot answer: “a critic who says the invariants measure our design choices rather than the model’s structure has a real point that we cannot fully answer.” Learned restriction maps are studied elsewhere on a fixed graph [BDCLB22; DBDL24]; the base space is not learned there.
problems.solved_when: A procedure and a published evaluation in which (i) planted sites in synthetic corpora are recovered up to a declared isomorphism budget, (ii) the site constructed from a natural corpus is stable under resampling within that budget, and (iii) invariants computed on it survive the gaming controls of [S02, §9.1] (terminal-site collapse, zero restrictions, filled nerve).

literature_check.finding: Sheaf neural networks with learned restriction maps on a given graph were found [BDCLB22; DBDL24]; no procedure that learns the site itself was found.

problems.title: The capability wager
problems.statement: On an orthogonal cellular sheaf the non-abelian holonomy capacity $\beta$ of [S02] is either $0$ or at least a constant $c(d)$ depending only on the stalk dimension. The wager is that $\beta$ governs capability. In the words of the source: “At matched parameters, data and compute, compare models with CERTIFIED_VIRTUALLY_ABELIAN and CERTIFIED_FREE reports on tasks requiring route-dependent evidence.” Decide the wager.
problems.established: The dichotomy is proved; the wager is not. “That β governs capability is grade D and we have no proof. It is the most interesting claim in the document and the least supported.” The comparison is set up so that a negative result costs only the wager: “No theorem links the verdict to capability; failure of the registered comparison removes the capability claim while leaving the group theorem intact.”
problems.background: The Tits alternative [Tit72]; uniform growth gaps [Bre11]; [HG19].
problems.solved_when: A preregistered comparison at matched parameters, data and compute, with certificates computed as in [S02, Ch. 3.6], published with its outcome in either direction.

literature_check.finding: No study linking holonomy growth of cellular sheaves to model capability was found.

problems.title: Nerve baselines between GRPO and RLOO
problems.statement: The source proves that the group-relative advantage of group relative policy optimisation (GRPO) [SWZ+24] equals $\Delta_0 R/\lVert\delta_0 R\rVert_2$ for the $0$-Laplacian of the nerve of the sampling group, wherever $\sigma>0$. This places GRPO in “a family of graph baselines indexed by a nerve, of which the complete-graph member is GRPO and the i.i.d. leave-one-out member is RLOO.” (RLOO is the leave-one-out REINFORCE baseline [ACG+24].) Determine whether another member of the family reduces the variance of the policy-gradient estimate at matched cost.
problems.established: The identity is proved and the family defined; “Whether any other member of that family reduces variance at matched cost is an open empirical question, tested by claim C11 of A7 and unanswered here.”
problems.background: [SWZ+24]; [ACG+24]; recent baselines for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards [ZZA+25].
problems.solved_when: A theorem identifying, under stated assumptions on rewards, a nerve whose baseline has strictly smaller variance than both GRPO and RLOO at matched sampling cost, or proving that no member of the family does; or the registered experiment C11 with its outcome.

literature_check.finding: Variance-reduction baselines for GRPO-type methods are an active topic [ZZA+25]; no study of the nerve family was found.

problems.title: Relative obstruction as a predictor of unsupported answers

source.title: GM-Omega-Infinity: Topos-Native Intelligence
source.status: T for the mathematics; D for what remains; N5 withdrawn

problems.statement: For an evidence subdomain $A\subseteq X$, a coefficient sheaf $F$ and a partial section $s_A$, the connecting class $\partial(s_A)\in H^1(X,A;F)$ is a genuine obstruction to extending $s_A$. Supply the typed record that the source requires before this class may be used as an instrument, and test prospectively whether it predicts unsupported answers of a language model.
problems.established: The mathematics is proved; the instrument is not: “N5 is therefore WITHDRAWN as a validation or falsification instrument.” Reinstatement requires six items, including “at least one worked non-zero example, together with a zero control, computed before labels are revealed”. The remaining task is stated as “What remains is the difficult empirical part: the evidence sheaf must reflect factual support, the relative class must be approximated at scale, and prospective prediction must beat entropy, retrieval sufficiency, self-consistency and correctness probes without site collapse.”
problems.solved_when: The six reinstatement items of §9.1.7 published for one benchmark, followed by a prospective comparison against entropy, sequence likelihood, verbal confidence, retrieval sufficiency, self-consistency and a trained correctness probe, reported in either direction.

literature_check.finding: Hallucination detectors based on entropy and probes exist [FKKG24]; sheaf-based consistency rating has been proposed [HRH24]; no instrument based on a relative connecting class was found.

problems.title: Topos-MoE against modern sparse mixture-of-experts
problems.statement: In Topos-MoE, the mixture-of-experts layer of [S02], each expert is an open sub-topos and routing constructs a sufficient cover. Run the registered comparison N7 of [S02, §9.1.9] against a modern fine-grained sparse mixture-of-experts at matched total and active parameters, executed FLOPs, wall time and communication. “Coverage routing must beat top-k on quality and on total cost; lowering its own deficiency score proves nothing about either.”
problems.established: The descent typing is proved; the benefit is not. In the released configuration the coverage router cannot yet be trained, and it “may not report the coverage router as a trained component until that backward exists and is finite-difference checked.” The thresholds are fixed in advance: “Confirmation requires a 10 per cent relative reduction in multi-expert composition error or a 3-point absolute improvement, while remaining within 1 per cent of the top-k baseline on single-expert tasks and within 10 per cent of its throughput.”
problems.solved_when: A trainable coverage router with a finite-difference-checked backward pass, and the N7 comparison executed under the registered protocol, reporting confirmation or one of the registered null outcomes.

literature_check.finding: Many routing variants for mixture-of-experts were found; none uses sheaf-theoretic coverage routing with these controls.

problems.title: A defence against a globally coherent falsehood

source.title: GM-Omega-Infinity: Topos-Native Intelligence
source.status: open (“we have no structural defence to propose”)

problems.statement: “Descent verification provably catches local inconsistency. Against a globally coherent falsehood it offers nothing, and we have no structural defence to propose.” Give a verification method that detects a stated class of globally coherent falsehoods, or prove that no verifier with access only to stated information can do so.
problems.established: The source proves the local guarantee and records the global gap as one of “The five things we are least sure of”; Part VI of [S02] discusses reward hacking at length without proposing a defence.
problems.solved_when: Either a method with a theorem stating which globally coherent falsehoods it detects and at what cost, evaluated on a published adversarial benchmark, or an impossibility theorem for a stated class of verifiers.

literature_check.finding: Consistency- and verification-based hallucination detection was found; no structural defence or impossibility theorem for globally coherent falsehoods was found.

problems.title: Compiled-to-streaming descent stability
problems.statement: Consider a session tower of finite certified sites and solid-valued states $(\mathcal C_n,P_n,F_n)_{n\ge 0}$ with the site maps of [S02, §2.2]. Conjecture 2.2.15: “If the cd-certificates are uniformly compatible under these site morphisms, the density bound is uniform, the coefficient towers satisfy the required derived-limit vanishing condition, and the finite probe systems form a conservative filtered family, then the limit state satisfies Nisnevich descent with solid condensed coefficients.” Prove or refute it.
problems.established: “The hypotheses are not discharged.” The source explains which hypotheses fail in practice — “Uniform density generally fails when new maximal atoms are added; derived-limit vanishing is not certified by the runtime; and no conservative finite probe family has been proved for arbitrary state classes” — and that “The conjecture therefore cannot be used to upgrade stagewise FINITE-ONLY certificates to a session-wide theorem.”
problems.background: Nisnevich descent [MV99]; condensed and solid mathematics [Sch19]; [Lur09].
problems.solved_when: A proof of the conjecture as stated, or a counterexample tower satisfying the four hypotheses whose limit state fails Nisnevich descent.

literature_check.finding: Work on descent for condensed and syntomic coefficients was found; no result on limits of towers of finite certified sites was found.

problems.title: The Beck–Chevalley square 12.6.3
problems.statement: For a context family $\mathrm{Rep}\colon\mathcal C_{\mathrm{ref}}\to\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, transport along refinements is coherent by straightening, but “Straightening supplies no Beck–Chevalley comparison for that square” formed by a refinement arrow and a cover restriction, and Proposition 2.4.24 shows that “The gap is real even in discrete categories.” Characterise the families and covers for which the comparison $\rho_V\circ r_!\Rightarrow (r_i)_!\circ\rho_U$ exists, is invertible, and satisfies the identity, composition and overlap coherence laws, so that the conditional Theorem 2.4.25 applies.
problems.established: Theorem 2.4.25 proves coverwise transport under exactly these hypotheses, and Chapter 13.5 audits finite fixtures; the source calls this “a scope restriction and conditional local closure, not a general solution.” “The monograph does not close the gap globally.”
problems.solved_when: A theorem giving necessary and sufficient conditions, in a stated generality, for the comparison of Theorem 2.4.25 to exist with its coherences, or a proof that no condition weaker than the hypothesis itself suffices in that generality.

literature_check.finding: Recent work on Beck–Chevalley fibrations concerns ambidexterity and norm squares; no result on refinement–cover squares of this kind was found.

problems.title: Sharp accumulation bounds for equivariance defects
problems.statement: The accumulation bound of [S02, Theorem 11.9.28] for the equivariance defects of successive layers is tight in the worst case, but its use as a certificate needs a lower bound on output norms that is not available. Question 11.11.18 asks: “Is there a class of architectures with certified lower norm control on which a usable ratio of bound to witness is O(1)? Failing that, is there a sharper bound that tracks the direction of the equivariance defect rather than only its magnitude, for instance by carrying a covariance rather than a scalar?”
problems.established: “Theorem 11.9.28 is tight in the worst case, with both of its constants attained.” Without the lower-norm premise the gate leaves the claim open: “A witness may still falsify a claim but cannot replace the missing certificate.” The source suggests, without attempting it, that defects may add in quadrature under a randomness assumption.
problems.background: Error accumulation in composed computations [Hig02]; equivariance in deep learning [BBCV21].
problems.solved_when: Either a class of architectures with certified lower norm control on which the ratio of bound to witness is proved O(1), or a direction-sensitive bound strictly sharper than Theorem 11.9.28 on a stated class, with proof.

literature_check.finding: No result of this form for equivariance defects was found.

problems.title: Local dynamics of the restriction-frame locus
problems.statement: Determine “whether the head-indexed restriction-frame embedded locus is attracting, repelling or a saddle under unfrozen frame dynamics”, the open entry O8 of the unproved register of [S02, Part P].
problems.established: Proposition 13.11.46 proves a parameter-specific departure from the locus and refutes universal invariance, but does not classify the local dynamics. The register names the missing tool: “a Lyapunov, centre-manifold or other local-dynamics argument for the frame manifold”.
problems.solved_when: A proof classifying the locus as attracting, repelling or a saddle (possibly depending on stated parameters) under the dynamics of Chapter 13.11.

literature_check.finding: Work on Stiefel-manifold training dynamics was found; no classification of this locus was found.

problems.title: A base-change bound for the descent solve
problems.statement: Prove “a base-change bound for the descent solve”: a bound relating the outputs of the descent solve of [S02, Ch. 13.10] at two bases, on which every cross-base stability statement of the book depends.
problems.established: The register records where the argument stops: “no bound relates the solve at two bases; the available Jacobian square measures a different quantity”.
problems.background: Spectral theory of sheaf Laplacians [HG19]; perturbation bounds [Hig02].
problems.solved_when: A proved bound, with explicit constants, on the difference of the descent solves at two bases in terms of a stated distance between the bases, or a family of examples showing that no such bound holds.

literature_check.finding: Work on sheaf diffusion and its stability was found; no base-change bound for this solve was found.

problems.title: The training-to-serving deviation
problems.statement: Prove that “the training-to-serving deviation is bounded” for the forward map of [S02, Ch. 13.10–13.11], or remove the failure: the register asks for “a proved bound, or a tie-break that removes the failure”.
problems.established: Bitwise equality between training and serving is proved under stated contracts and fails outside them: “equality fails through the tie-break under rounding; no bound on the output difference is proved”.
problems.solved_when: A proved bound on the output difference between training and serving under the rounding model of Chapter 13.11, or a tie-break rule with a proof that it restores equality.

literature_check.finding: Engineering work on deterministic inference was found [ZDY+25]; no proved bound for this forward map was found.

problems.title: Monotone refinement budgets
problems.statement: The recomputed refinement budget of [S02, Proposition 11.9.20] is not monotone along refinement. Question 11.11.19: “Is there a natural class of covers — closed under the refinements one actually performs — on which some useful instrument is monotone?” The source names two candidate classes, nerve-preserving refinements and split-only refinements.
problems.established: For both candidates the needed facts are unproved, and “No such theorem is currently available.” A proved monotone direction would let the diameter of a totally ordered class be read at its endpoints.
problems.solved_when: A theorem identifying such a class and an instrument monotone on it, or a proof that each of the two named classes admits no useful monotone instrument.

literature_check.finding: No result on monotone instruments under cover refinement was found.

problems.title: How many ambiguity axes are there?
problems.statement: The indeterminacy calculus of [S02, Ch. 11.9] separates the ways a reported number can depend on arbitrary choices. “Chapter 11.9 opened with three and closed with four: the comparison link of Definition 11.9.42 was found only after the first three had been written up, which is evidence that the enumeration is incomplete.” Determine whether routing tie-breaking is a fifth axis with useful exact invariants, and whether the enumeration is complete.
problems.established: “Whether tie rules form a separate typed transformation family with useful exact invariants remains open; no fifth calculus is asserted.” Simplicial orientation and numerical precision are examined and dismissed with reasons.
problems.solved_when: A typed transformation family for tie rules with its exact invariants, or a proof that tie rules reduce to the four existing axes; a completeness theorem for a stated class of instruments also solves the problem.

literature_check.finding: No result on this classification was found.

problems.title: Second-order disagreement without engineering
problems.statement: “On a graph, and under standard top-k routing, H2 vanishes identically.” The degree-two (gerbe) theory of disagreement among experts is therefore vacuous unless the cover is built for it: “The minimal non-vacuous configuration is four experts arranged as ∂Δ3, and it must be engineered deliberately.” Determine whether covers produced by a data-driven routing or cover-construction procedure, on natural tasks, carry non-zero second cohomology with the coefficient data of [S02].
problems.established: The source proves the vanishing results and warns that “engineering a structure into existence in order to measure it is a move that deserves suspicion.” A gerbe diagnostic is “vacuous unless the cover has a deliberate, data-justified sparse nerve with genuine two-dimensional cycles and explicitly defined coefficient data.”
problems.solved_when: A procedure, not tuned to produce two-cycles, whose covers on a published natural task carry a certified non-zero class in degree two; or a theorem that a stated class of procedures always yields vanishing second cohomology.

literature_check.finding: No result on second cohomology of routing nerves was found.

problems.title: Formalizing uniform circuit classes

source.title: GM-Omega-Infinity: Topos-Native Intelligence
source.locator: Open Problem 13.15.B, p. 3135; cut ledger, Table 13.15.7, p. 3133

problems.statement: “Formalise L-uniform circuit families and the AC$^0$ many-one reduction convention of Definition 2.14.5 to the point where clauses 4 and 5 of Theorem 13.13.24 become statable, and decide whether the Barrington construction of Chapter 2.14 is within reach of a proof term.”
problems.established: The source’s separation results use L-uniform circuit classes and Barrington’s theorem on paper; the machine-checked part stops at statements, and the cut ledger records that “a Barrington formalisation is a project in itself”.
problems.background: [Bar89]; [BIS90]; a recent Lean formalisation of the non-uniform PARITY lower bound [Wes26].
problems.solved_when: A Lean (or other assistant) library defining L-uniform circuit families and AC$^0$ many-one reductions in which clauses 4 and 5 of Theorem 13.13.24 are stated, together with either a formal proof of Barrington’s theorem or a documented estimate of what such a proof requires.

literature_check.finding: The non-uniform PARITY lower bound has been formalised in Lean [Wes26]; uniformity and Barrington’s theorem were not found in mathlib or in formal-conjectures (GitHub code search).

problems.title: A second kernel
problems.statement: “Establish whether an independent type-checker covers the features used by the 13.11 and 13.13 developments, and if so make REPLAYED require two kernels rather than two machines.” Independent checkers for Lean 4 now exist [Car24; nanoda]; the problem is to elaborate the Lean declarations of [S02, Table 13.15.1] at a pinned toolchain and replay them under Lean’s kernel and under an independent checker.
problems.established: In the release no declaration was elaborated, and the source says of its replay status: “The present definition of REPLAYED is weaker than the name suggests, and this is stated rather than hidden.”
problems.solved_when: The declarations elaborated at a pinned toolchain and replayed by two independent kernels, with a report of the features used and of any declaration that one kernel rejects.

literature_check.finding: Independent Lean 4 checkers were found [Car24; nanoda]; the Lean 4 repository contains a replay checker and an export format (src/LeanChecker.lean, src/LeanExport; GitHub code search, leanprover/lean4). No replay of these declarations was found.

problems.title: The computational-univalence bridge
problems.statement: Build the checker of Hypothesis CU-MJ of [S02]: “There exists an approved external checker that: 1. represents proof-relevant paths and a univalent universe independently of Lean equality; 2. computes coercion along equivalences using cubical composition or an equivalent certified mechanism; 3. checks the higher coherences required by the transported family; 4. emits a replayable term rather than a Boolean success flag;” and 5. binds that term to the canonical target, equivalence, site, cover, universe and checker of the justification being transported.
problems.established: “No such integrated component is supplied by this chapter, so CU-MJ is graded X.” Every theorem that assumes it is conditional; the finite branch of the chapter does not need it.
problems.solved_when: A checker satisfying the five clauses, and one transported justification from [S02, Ch. 4.7] checked end to end with its replayable term published.

literature_check.finding: Cubical proof assistants and proof-transfer tools exist [CCHM18; VMA21]; no checker bound to Lean targets in the sense of clause 5 was found.

problems.title: Polarization of a cyclotomic spectrum

source.title: Arithmetic Spectral Descent
source.locator: Problem 24.18, p. 539 (restated as Problems 29.8 and 30.16); Criterion 57.5, p. 1145

problems.statement: Define a polarization of a cyclotomic spectrum: extra data on Real topological Hochschild homology (THR) $(\mathrm{THR}(R),O(2),\{\varphi^{\mathbb R}_p\})$, generalising an ample class or a Kähler form, such that (i) it induces a real quadratic form on $\pi_*(\mathrm{THR}(R)^{hO(2)})$ through a trace state; (ii) “the form is definite on primitive parts with respect to a Lefschetz decomposition”; and (iii) for $X$ smooth projective over $\mathbb F_q$ with an ample line bundle, “it recovers the Hodge index theorem on crystalline cohomology / the positivity underlying the Weil conjectures.”
problems.established: The source explains why (iii) is already delicate: crystalline cohomology carries no real structure, and the Katz–Messing comparison transports eigenvalues but not the positivity mechanism. Criterion 57.5 fixes a test: a proposed polarization solves the problem only if, applied to the topological Hochschild homology $\mathrm{THH}(C)$ of a curve $C$ over $\mathbb F_q$ of genus $g\ge1$, it proves $|\alpha_i|=\sqrt q$ for the inverse roots of the numerator of $Z(C,t)$ without invoking Weil’s theorem, Riemann–Roch on $C\times C$ or the Hodge index theorem.
problems.solved_when: A definition satisfying (i)–(iii), with the test of Criterion 57.5 passed for every curve over a finite field. The bound $|\alpha_i|=\sqrt q$ is a theorem (Weil); the problem is to obtain it from the new structure.

literature_check.finding: Work on Real topological Hochschild homology and its cyclotomic structure was found [DMPR21]; no notion of polarization of the required kind was found.

problems.title: Construction Problem A1 on the syntomic stack
problems.statement: Construct, on quasi-coherent sheaves on the syntomic stack $\mathbb Z_p^{\mathrm{syn}}$ (equivalently on $F$-gauges over $\mathbb Z_p$), a $\mathbb C$-linear endomorphism $\Theta$ of the underlying object after $\otimes_{W,\iota}\mathbb C$ such that (A1.1) on the Hodge–Tate locus $\Theta=-\tfrac{2\pi i}{\log q}\Theta_{\mathrm{Sen}}$ for objects pulled back from $\mathbb F_q$; (A1.2) $q^\Theta=\mathrm{Fr}_q^*$ for $F$-gauges coming from smooth proper $X/\mathbb F_q$; (A1.3) $\Theta$ is $\mathbb C$-linear, which “rules out semilinear operators”; and (A1.4) the regularized determinant $\det_\infty(s-\Theta)$ on motivic cohomology converges and equals $\zeta(X,s)$.
problems.established: The source isolates the difficulty in (A1.3): the Frobenius part of $\Theta$ is semilinear over $W$, and over $\mathbb Z_p$ no power of $\varphi$ is $W$-linear. “The syntomic stack exists, but the operator on it does not—yet.”
problems.solved_when: A construction satisfying (A1.1)–(A1.4), or a proof that no endomorphism with (A1.1)–(A1.3) exists.

literature_check.finding: The Sen operator on the Hodge–Tate stack is known [BL22; Dri20]; no operator with (A1.1)–(A1.4) was found.

problems.title: Archimedean Frobenius from quaternionic THH

source.title: Arithmetic Spectral Descent
source.status: O (first half answered since; see the literature check)

problems.statement: Problem 28.13 of [S03] asks two questions. The first — whether there is “a lift of THH to genuine Pin(2)-spectra rather than O(2)-spectra” — has been answered: quaternionic topological Hochschild homology THQ, defined for rings with twisted $C_4$-action, carries a $\mathrm{Pin}(2)$-action [AMP26]. The second remains: is its $\mathrm{Pin}(2)$-homotopy fixed-point theory “the correct 𝜑∞ for symplectically self-dual motives, with 𝑂(2) handling the orthogonal ones?” Concretely, determine whether $\mathrm{THQ}(R)^{h\mathrm{Pin}(2)}$ carries an operator $\Theta_\infty$ satisfying the analogue of requirement (C′1) of Construction 28.14 — its half-line spectrum, with Hodge multiplicities, gives the archimedean local factors of symplectically self-dual motives by $\det_\infty((s-\Theta_\infty)/2\pi)$.
problems.established: The source calls the question “a well-posed question in equivariant stable homotopy theory, independent of RH”, and states that “No existing construction is known”; that statement is corrected here (it is recorded in the errata of the repository). Construction 28.14 lists the requirements (C′1)–(C′4) for the orthogonal case.
problems.solved_when: An operator on $\mathrm{THQ}(R)^{h\mathrm{Pin}(2)}$ for a stated class of rings with the required structure, with a proof of the analogue of (C′1) for symplectically self-dual motives in that class; or a proof that no natural operator can satisfy it.

literature_check.finding: Found: Angelini-Knoll, Merling and Péroux construct THQ with its Pin(2)-action (arXiv:2409.18187, 2024; Adv. Math. 2026) [AMP26]. This answers the first question of Problem 28.13; no work on the second was found.

problems.title: A certified inertia for the pole-removed Weil form

source.title: Arithmetic Spectral Descent
source.locator: Criterion 58.9 (falsification predicate F2), p. 1169; Proposition 46.5 and Remark 46.13, pp. xxxv, 919

problems.statement: For sixty-three cubic-spline test spaces $V_{T,N}$ ($0.15\le T\le 3$, $4\le N\le 64$) the source measured, in floating point with tolerance $10^{-9}$, that the pole-removed Weil form $B_N=W_N-P_N$ has inertia $(N-1,1)$. Certify this measurement in interval or exact arithmetic for each configuration — certify $N-1$ positive eigenvalues and exhibit a vector $z$ with a certified enclosure of $B_N(z,z)<0$ — or show for some configuration that the certified inertia differs, which is falsification predicate F2 of [S03, Criterion 58.9].
problems.established: Under RH the full Weil form is positive semidefinite and $n_-(B_N)\le1$ (Corollary 46.11); the lower bound $n_-(B_N)\ge1$ is not proved conditionally or otherwise (Warning 46.12). The measurement is finite evidence: “What the data exclude is a large second negative direction. What they do not exclude is a small one.” F2 asks for “the computation certified in interval arithmetic”.
problems.background: Weil positivity at the archimedean place [CC21]; interval arithmetic [Joh17]; certified computation of zeta zeros [PT21]; certification for other finite truncations of the Weil form [Gro26].
problems.solved_when: Certified inertia for all sixty-three configurations of Proposition 46.5, with the code and the enclosures published; a configuration whose certified inertia is not $(N-1,1)$ also solves the problem, by firing F2. The result is a statement about finitely many matrices; it is not evidence for or against RH.

literature_check.finding: A certification rule and an interval factorization for the Galerkin truncations of the Weil quadratic form of Connes, van Suijlekom, Consani and Moscovici were found [Gro26]; no certified computation of the inertia of the Gram matrices of these sixty-three test spaces was found.

problems.title: The Tamagawa factor as a local term
problems.statement: The source proposes three constructions of the bad-prime term $c_p$ of the conjecture of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer: a vertical intersection multiplicity on the arithmetic surface, a Lefschetz–Verdier term of a fixed-point stack, and a determinant defect of the prismatic/Néron component lattice. Problem 22.7.1: “Construct the three local objects just described and prove that each has Euler characteristic c_p, compatibly with change of model, Frobenius action, and the integral orientation of the fundamental line.”
problems.established: The identification of $c_p$ as a Lefschetz–Verdier local term is listed among the book’s novelties, and the source fixes the test: “This is a particularly useful falsification test. Tate’s algorithm gives c_p independently for every database curve. If a proposed prismatic or fixed-point formula disagrees even once, that local construction is wrong. No appeal to BSD can repair such a disagreement.” The book lists this among the items that are “testable now, independently of BSD.”
problems.solved_when: The three constructions with proofs that each has Euler characteristic $c_p$ with the stated compatibilities; or a curve and a prime at which a proposed construction disagrees with Tate’s algorithm, which refutes that construction. The problem concerns local terms and does not bear on the truth of BSD.

literature_check.finding: No prismatic or fixed-point formula for the Tamagawa factor was found.

problems.title: The arithmetic flow
problems.statement: Construct a strongly continuous flow on a cohomology theory over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$ whose primitive closed orbits are the primes, the orbit at $p$ having length $\log p$, with no spurious orbits and with a generator satisfying the weight adjunction. In the form of Problem 4.5.1: a foliated or laminated space with a flow and a leafwise cohomology admitting duality and regularized determinants, whose Lefschetz trace formula is the explicit formula.
problems.established: “The flow Φ𝑡 is postulated, not built. No ℝ≥0-action has ever been constructed on any cohomology theory over Specℤ whose primitive closed orbits are the primes with lengths log p”. For Problem 4.5.1: “No object satisfying these requirements is presently known.” The cyclotomic structure of THH supplies $\psi_p$ at each prime; the interpolation to a continuous action is missing.
problems.proposed_by: Deninger [Den98]; restated, with the source’s axioms, in [S04].
problems.solved_when: A construction with the stated properties, or a no-go theorem showing that no $\mathbb R_{\ge0}$-action of the required kind exists on any cohomology of $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$ (item (ii) of the refutation list of [S04, §2.8.1]).

literature_check.finding: Trace formulas for foliated flows and regularized-determinant formulas in Deninger’s framework were found; no construction over Spec ℤ was found.

problems.title: Sub-conductor rank detection
problems.statement: Does there exist a natural family $\mathcal F_X$ of elliptic curves, a function $P(X)=X^{o(1)}$, and explicit statistics $S_X$ depending only on $\{a_p(E): p\le P(X)\}$, such that the conditional laws of $S_X$ for analytic rank $0$, $1$ and at least $2$ have distinct non-degenerate limits after the root number and all known local confounders are matched?
problems.established: The source explains the clause on confounders: “The matching clause matters. Without it, a classifier may merely learn the functional-equation sign or a database convention.” Either answer is informative: “A positive answer would ask for a new family trace formula; a negative answer would also be informative by locating the finite-sample origin of the observed signal.”
problems.background: [HLOP22]; [Zub23]; [BKLPR15]; neural rank prediction from Frobenius traces [BCD+26].
problems.solved_when: A theorem establishing distinct limits for a stated family and statistic with $P(X)=X^{o(1)}$, or a theorem that no statistic of this kind separates the ranks after matching.

literature_check.finding: Machine-learning prediction of analytic rank from Frobenius traces has been reported with high accuracy [BCD+26] and murmurations studied [HLOP22; Zub23]; no theorem of the requested form, with the matching clause, was found.

problems.title: Murmurations from the flow: a falsification test
problems.statement: If the framework of [S04] is correct, the murmuration density arises as a transition term in its Lefschetz–Verdier localisation, and three computable predictions follow: (i) $y=p/N$ is the natural coordinate, and no other combination of $p$ and $N$ appears in the leading term; (ii) the density for elliptic curves, if it exists, has the same oscillation frequencies as the modular-form density $M_2$; (iii) the rank-conditioned densities are governed by the same density with the root number replaced by the Selmer fixed-point class. Carry out the tests.
problems.established: “Each clause is falsifiable by computation. Clause (i) fails if any family shows a leading term depending on p and N other than through p/N; clause (ii) fails if the observed elliptic-curve frequencies differ from those of M2.” The protocol is in Chapter 55.
problems.solved_when: The tests of clauses (i) and (ii) carried out under the protocol of [S04, Ch. 55] against the densities of [Zub23] and [SS25], with data and code published and the outcome reported in either direction; clause (iii) when the Selmer class is computable.

literature_check.finding: A conjectural explicit murmuration density for elliptic curves ordered by height has been given [SS25], and murmurations have been derived from ratios conjectures [Cow24]; these supply what clause (ii) is tested against. No test of the three clauses was found.

problems.title: The Hodge decomposition in Lean

source.title: The Archimedean Prism
source.locator: Problem 71.11.1, p. 1027; dossier, p. 1034; The five volumes, p. xv

problems.statement: “Formalise the Hodge decomposition for compact Kähler manifolds in Lean 4 with mathlib, the single largest absent prerequisite identified in Chapter 64.”
problems.established: The source records the verdict that “the Hodge conjecture cannot presently even be stated in Lean 4 with mathlib”, and estimates the formalisation “as an effort on the order of the Liquid Tensor Experiment.” Its dossier limits what success means: “Success would enable formal statements of the later conjectures; it would prove none of them by itself.” Problem 71.11.2 (Chow groups and the cycle class map) is the other missing prerequisite.
problems.solved_when: A Lean 4 development, accepted into Mathlib or released as a library building against it, that defines compact Kähler manifolds and proves the Hodge decomposition of their de Rham cohomology.

literature_check.finding: GitHub code search (2026-10-28) found in mathlib a Hodge star on exterior powers and algebraic Kähler differentials, but no Kähler manifolds and no Hodge decomposition; formal-conjectures contains no Hodge-theoretic statement.

problems.title: No δ-structure on the archimedean prism
problems.statement: “Make precise, as a no-go theorem, the claim that the archimedean prism carries no 𝛿-structure and hence no literal Frobenius lift.”
problems.established: “Chapter 16 argues the analogy with prismatic cohomology is structural only; a no-go theorem would settle the point rather than assert it.” The dossier sets the standard: “A no-go theorem must quantify over all functorial candidate operations and identify an invariant they cannot satisfy; observing that the current construction lacks one is not enough.”
problems.solved_when: A theorem that quantifies over all functorial operations on the archimedean prism of [S05, Ch. 13–17] in a stated sense and proves that none is a δ-structure (or a Frobenius lift), by exhibiting an invariant that every such operation would have to satisfy and does not; or a functorial δ-structure, which would refute the claim.

literature_check.finding: No result on δ-structures for archimedean or real Hodge-theoretic analogues of prisms was found.

problems.title: Independence of the twelve prism axioms
problems.statement: “Prove that the twelve prism axioms AP1–AP12 are logically independent by exhibiting, for each, a model satisfying the other eleven and failing it.”
problems.established: “Theorem 46.4.1 states the axioms; their independence is asserted but not demonstrated.” The dossier: “The twelve axioms are individually motivated, but motivation does not prove logical independence.”
problems.background: Hodge theory [Del71]; the axioms and their sources are in [S05, Ch. 46].
problems.solved_when: Twelve models, the $k$-th satisfying every axiom except AP$k$, each verified against the definitions of [S05, Ch. 46]; or a proof that one axiom follows from the others, which is a correction to the source.

literature_check.finding: No work on these axioms outside [S05] was found.

problems.title: Descent beyond the polarized case
problems.statement: “Determine whether the descent theorem Theorem 15.4.2 holds for non-polarisable mixed Hodge structures, or exhibit the first obstruction to it.”
problems.established: In the source, “descent along the prism is proved only in the polarised pure case.” The dossier explains what changes: “Nonpolarisable mixed structures have nonsemisimple extension data and weight filtrations that need not split; automorphism groupoids can cease to be reductive”, and notes that the answer may be a counterexample rather than an extension theorem.
problems.solved_when: A proof of the descent theorem for non-polarisable mixed Hodge structures in a stated class, or an explicit mixed Hodge structure for which descent fails, with the obstruction identified.

literature_check.finding: No result on descent along the archimedean prism was found outside [S05].

problems.title: A prism reading of Voisin’s counterexample
problems.statement: “Compute the prism obstruction class of Voisin’s 2002 Weil-torus counterexample and verify that it is exactly the projectivity obstruction, not a new one.”
problems.established: “Theorem 37.2.4 predicts the counterexample strikes at the projectivity step; an explicit computation would confirm the negation of falsifier F8.” Voisin’s examples [Voi02] show that the Hodge conjecture fails for compact Kähler manifolds that are not projective.
problems.solved_when: An explicit computation of the prism obstruction class for the tori of [Voi02], showing that it is the projectivity obstruction of [S05, Theorem 37.2.4]; a computation showing that it is a different class refutes the prediction.

literature_check.finding: No prism-theoretic analysis of Voisin’s examples was found outside [S05].

problems.title: Close the formal algebra leaf

source.title: Strained Prismatic Geometry
source.locator: Problem 62.1.5 (rank 2 of the critical path), p. 1275

problems.statement: With pinned Lean and Mathlib versions, “Discharge PO-090 with definitions whose types separate a p-derivation from an ordinary derivation, proofs of the sum and product identities including p = 2, compatibility with the induced Frobenius lift, executable regression examples, no admitted declarations, and an axiom report containing only the approved logical foundations.”
problems.established: “This ranks second because the mathematics is known and the acceptance test is finite.” Failures of tooling do not count against the mathematics: “A library or elaboration failure is an engineering result, not a refutation.” The repository gives the statements in Lean (formal/GrothendieckianProblems/P49.lean).
problems.solved_when: Proofs of the statements in formal/GrothendieckianProblems/P49.lean, with no sorry, no new axioms, and the regression examples of PO-090, checked at the pinned toolchain.

literature_check.finding: GitHub code search (2026-10-28) found no δ-ring or p-derivation in mathlib.

problems.title: Toward an algorithm for prismatic cohomology
problems.statement: “There is presently no general terminating algorithm which, from equations for an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme, computes its absolute prismatic cohomology together with derived completion, Nygaard filtration, Frobenius, and effective descent as an F-gauge”. “The frontier relevant to this book has five layers”: absolute descent; integral semistable gauges for curves with bad reduction, including the primes 2 and 3; the Habiro–prismatic comparison; archimedean assembly; and the global strain trace. Give a terminating, certified algorithm for one layer.
problems.established: The companion package of [S06] supplies finite inputs and hard failure states, and “implements none of these by renaming a local matrix.”
problems.solved_when: A terminating algorithm for one of the five layers on a stated class of inputs, with a proof of correctness and an implementation whose outputs agree with known computations.

literature_check.finding: Explicit computations of prismatic and syntomic cohomology in special cases were found; no general algorithm for any of the five layers was found.

problems.title: The real-place gauge

source.title: Strained Prismatic Geometry
source.locator: Problem 62.1.7 (rank 4 of the critical path), p. 1276

problems.statement: In the analytic-stack and condensed setting of [S06, Ch. 17], “Construct the gauge stack of PO-017; prove the uniqueness, finite-place compatibility, coherent all-place gluing, Arakelov degree comparison, and exceptional-operation functoriality of PO-018–PO-022; and settle the archimedean coefficient overlap and dualisability issues represented by PO-097–PO-098.”
problems.established: The target is typed but no existence theorem is available. The source gives the falsifier: “A non-zero principal-rescaling defect, failure of real descent, or failure of dualisability for the required leg destroys this version of the all-place assembly.”
problems.solved_when: A construction with proofs of PO-017–PO-022 and PO-097–PO-098, or an instance of one of the three named falsifiers.

literature_check.finding: No construction of an archimedean gauge stack of this kind was found.

problems.title: The gluing problem for the global substrate
problems.statement: Construct an analytic stack $\mathfrak S$ with morphisms $\mathfrak S_v\to\mathfrak S$ for every place $v$ of $\mathbb Q$ and a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z\to\mathfrak S$ such that (i) $D(\mathfrak S)$ maps to $D(\mathfrak S_v)$ for every $v$, compatibly with the rational realisations; (ii) the local structures — Frobenius and Nygaard filtration at finite $v$, weight filtration and dilation at $\infty$ — are matched by the comparison data; and (iii) $\mathfrak S$ is not terminal.
problems.established: “Condition (iii) is what makes the problem non-trivial: a terminal object satisfies (i) and (ii) vacuously.” The legs can be compared only through $\mathbb Q$ (Remark 18.1.4), and Obstruction 18.1.6 shows that a Frobenius datum on a glued object degenerates at infinity.
problems.solved_when: A construction satisfying (i)–(iii), or a proof that every analytic stack satisfying (i) and (ii) is terminal.

literature_check.finding: No construction of this kind was found.

problems.title: The multiplicative-group gate
problems.statement: Let $\mathrm{Bun}^{\mathrm{ar}}_{\mathbb G_m}$ be the arithmetic Picard stack of the global arithmetic curve $\mathfrak X_{\mathbb Z}$ of [S07] and $\mathrm{Gauge}$ its category of gauge sheaves. Construct them and prove or refute that $\zeta(\mathrm{TC}(\Phi\mid\mathrm{Gauge}(\mathrm{Bun}^{\mathrm{ar}}_{\mathbb G_m})),s)=\pi^{-s/2} \Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$, the completed Riemann zeta function, with the archimedean factor produced by the archimedean chart and not inserted.
problems.established: The source calls this “the primary go/no-go test for the framework”: “If the framework yields anything else — in particular, if it yields 𝜁(𝑠) without the Γ-factor, or with a Γ-factor of the wrong argument — then it is wrong, and no amount of repair at higher strata will save it.” “This criterion is designated for formal verification; its current status is recorded in Appendix F.”
problems.solved_when: A construction of the objects in the abelian case and a proof of the displayed identity, or a proof that the construction yields a different function, which refutes the framework as stated. The completed zeta function and its functional equation are classical; the problem is whether this construction produces them.

literature_check.finding: No construction of the arithmetic Picard stack of this framework was found outside [S07].

problems.title: The first falsification test for GL$_2$
problems.statement: “For the standard GL2 monoid over Q, construct a global distribution on the rank-one stratum whose local normal residue is the coefficient of” Proposition 28.16 of [S07], “and prove that its spectral expansion is exactly the sum of the trivial, special, and maximal-parabolic terms removed in Altuğ’s Poisson reorganisation.”
problems.established: A mismatch of coefficients would refute the simplest form of the source’s Conjecture 28.20. The problem precedes functoriality on purpose: “It asks whether the diagnosis reproduces a known rank-one calculation without changing its constants. A framework that cannot pass this comparison has no claim on the general problem.”
problems.solved_when: The distribution constructed and its spectral expansion proved equal to the terms removed in [Alt15], or a proof that the coefficients differ.

literature_check.finding: Altuğ’s Beyond Endoscopy computations for GL$_2$ over the rationals [Alt15] and their extension to totally real fields, which removes the trivial and special representations by Poisson summation on the regular elliptic terms [EEKW24], were found; no boundary-resolution reading of them was found.

problems.title: Ambidexterity over the arithmetic base
problems.statement: Let $q\colon\mathrm{Bun}_G(\mathfrak X_{\mathbb Z})\to\mathrm{pt}$ be the structure map. Prove or refute that $q_!\simeq q_*$ on $\mathrm{Shv}_{\mathcal N}(\mathrm{Bun}_G(\mathfrak X_{\mathbb Z}))$ after Whittaker renormalisation; if the equivalence holds only after a renormalisation, identify it explicitly and determine whether it is canonical.
problems.established: “This is the load-bearing hypothesis of the entire framework.” Over a curve the corresponding statement, miraculous duality, is a theorem of Drinfeld and Gaitsgory; over $\mathfrak X_{\mathbb Z}$ the local finiteness its proof uses is unavailable. “It is also the gap about which the least can currently be said.”
problems.proposed_by: [S07]; over a curve the source cites miraculous duality as a theorem of Drinfeld and Gaitsgory; see [Gai18] and [AGK+20].
problems.solved_when: A proof or a refutation of the equivalence, with the renormalisation identified if one is needed.

literature_check.finding: Miraculous duality and duality for automorphic sheaves over curves were found [Gai18; AGK+20]; no arithmetic analogue was found.

problems.title: Construct the global arithmetic curve
problems.statement: Exhibit a condensed analytic stack over the sphere spectrum satisfying the eight clauses of the definition of the global arithmetic curve $\mathfrak X_{\mathbb Z}$ [S07, Definition 10.15] — finite syntomic charts, an archimedean chart, a restricted adelic halo with a rational diagonal, the gluing as a homotopy fibre product, an absolute Frobenius, a gauge map to $\mathbb A^1/\mathbb G_m$, a place map to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z$, and a fundamental class in degree three — prove it unique up to canonical equivalence, and equip it with a six-functor formalism with proper base change and Verdier duality.
problems.established: “What exists at present is a specification and two of its charts.” The finite charts are theorems of Bhatt–Lurie and Drinfeld; the archimedean chart is stipulated. “The obstacle is not the charts. It is the gluing, and the reason is specific. Adelic descent along a restricted product is not a standard operation in any existing formalism.”
problems.solved_when: A construction with the eight clauses, the uniqueness statement and the six-functor formalism, or a proof that no object satisfies the eight clauses.

literature_check.finding: No construction of this kind was found.

problems.title: Coherence for arithmetic modes
problems.statement: For the modal directed type theory $\mathrm{TT}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\mathrm{KH}}$ of [S07, Ch. 6], construct a finite presentation of its mode two-category and “prove a coherence theorem deciding equality of generated two-cells”, while retaining the Beck–Chevalley, projection-formula, place-commutation, Frobenius and $\flat\dashv\sharp$ structures of the chapter.
problems.established: “A positive solution would not construct the semantic functors, but it would make their formal composites manageable. A negative solution would force a proof-relevant representation of coherence cells in the kernel and would weaken the decidability prospect.”
problems.solved_when: A finite presentation and a coherence theorem with a decision procedure for equality of generated two-cells, mechanised or proved on paper with all cases, or a proof that equality is undecidable for every finite presentation retaining the listed structures.

literature_check.finding: Multimodal type theory [GKNB21] and its normalization theorem, which reduces conversion to the conversion problem of the mode theory and gives decidable type checking for a decidable mode theory [Gra22], were found; no coherence theorem for these modes was found.
